acts.name: The first predictions
acts.desc: Charles Russell's magazine set dates for the end, and the dates came and went

acts.name: New leaders, new rules
acts.desc: More dates, a ban on blood transfusions, and the organization's own Bible

acts.name: What came out later
acts.desc: Redefinitions, the UN membership, and what a royal commission found in their files

turningPoints.1914: Armageddon was due and war came instead; the date was kept and its meaning rewritten
turningPoints.1945: Blood transfusions were forbidden, a rule the movement had not held for its first 65 years
turningPoints.1954–64: Worship of Jesus, taught since 1898 and written into the charter, was declared unscriptural
turningPoints.1975: Members sold homes for a date the organization later admitted its own publications had built
turningPoints.2012: Eight men reinterpreted the verse that grants their authority to mean the eight of them
turningPoints.2015–16: An Australian inquiry found 1,006 alleged abusers in their files and not one reported
